rejected.title: Shape of a distribution
card: The shape of a distribution is the pattern made when you display data, such as in a dot plot or stem-and-leaf plot. A display makes the pattern easy to see.
Symmetric
the two sides of the display look like mirror images of each other. Skewed: the data bunches up on one side and has a long tail on the other. The skew is named after the tail.
Cluster
a group of values close together. Gap: a stretch with no values. Outlier: a value far from the rest.
Example: quiz scores of 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9 have most values bunched at 4 to 7, with a tail towards 9. The tail points to the higher scores, so the data is skewed to the right.
rejected.remember: Look for the tail to name a skew, and look for clusters, gaps and outliers.

a.q: Most students in a class read 3 to 6 books in a term. A few read 15 or more. How is the data shaped?
opts: Skewed, with a long tail towards the high values
Skewed, with a long tail towards the low values
Symmetric, with the same spread on both sides
Symmetric, with a gap in the middle of the data
a.why: Most values bunch at the low end and a few high values stretch out the right side. The long tail is towards the high values, so it is skewed that way. It is not symmetric, because the two sides are not mirror images.
a.clue: Which way does the long tail point?

b.q: Ten students' times to run 100 m, in seconds, are 15, 16, 16, 17, 17, 18, 18, 19, 20 and 31. Which statement about the data is correct?
opts: 31 is an outlier, far from the rest of the times
31 is part of a cluster with the other times
There is a gap between 15 and 16 in the data
The data is symmetric, as 31 balances the 15
b.why: Nine times lie between 15 and 20, and 31 is far from all of them, so it is an outlier. The only gap is between 20 and 31, not between 15 and 16. One extreme value does not make the data symmetric, because it stretches a tail out to the high side.
b.clue: Compare the jump from 20 to 31 with the other jumps.
